title: The kb-autopilot skill runs one manager tick under /loop
goal: New .claude/skills/kb-autopilot/SKILL.md, run in the manager's own clone under /loop, does one tick from python3 _tools/autopilot.py status: backlog.py intake --file --network and triage of its drafts; for each runner that exited (status names its cause), the sprint's review, retrospective and close, its provisional answers confirmed and its retro stories picked as autopilot decisions (answer --by autopilot --record, never a secrets or push gate); a refill to two runners (plan, research, start, then autopilot.py runner start in the background, whose pid from autopilot.py status the tick records with backlog.py procs --record, and backlog.py procs --end for owned orphans); the digest; and a PushNotification only for gates the operator keeps (blocking gates of a class the autopilot may not answer). Judgment steps (triage, review, retrospective, plan) run in subagents that return one short JSON object each, named in the skill with its keys; the skill holds a Compact Instructions section and never writes auto-memory. AGENTS.md lists /kb-autopilot and stays under its 4 KB cap (bytes removed elsewhere in it, meaning kept). A test file test_autopilot_skill.py (tests named autopilot_skill_*) checks that the skill is well formed, that each command it names exists (its subcommand parses with --help), that it names the subagent JSON keys, Compact Instructions and PushNotification only for kept gates, and that it holds no instruction to write memory, each with a planted failure. .claude/settings.json is not changed unless the goal's loop needs it, and then never a permission rule.
